name: WebTransport
plain: Opens low-latency streams and datagrams to an HTTP/3 server, with no prompt.
meaning: A site can send and receive many parallel streams and unreliable datagrams over QUIC. Faster than WebSockets, but also a flexible channel for covert upload.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

limits.headline: Can open fast two way streams to a server, with no pop up
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, like a live video or game.
can: Send and get many streams of data at once
Send small quick messages with low delay
Keep the link open while the page is open
cannot: Work with a server that does not support HTTP/3
Stay connected after you close the tab
Work in Safari, including on iPhone, where it is not available yet
Reach your files or other apps
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Firefox support it. Safari does not yet.

story.what_it_is: A newer, faster live line to a server, with no prompt.

marketing.name: WebTransport
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say WebTransport offers low delay two way streams and datagrams over HTTP/3.

story.for_you: You never see it. It makes cloud games, live video and fast apps feel quicker, especially on shaky wifi.
story.for_makers: Makers get lower delay than older live lines and can send things out of order, which is perfect for games where old data is useless. It is the next step beyond WebSockets.

use_cases.example: A cloud game or a fast browser shooter sends controller and move data as quick datagrams, so a lost packet does not stall the game.
A live sports stream delivers video with sub second delay.
A conferencing tool sends media over HTTP/3 and recovers faster from poor networks.
A shared whiteboard syncs strokes with very low delay.
A telemetry tool streams many small events without blocking.
A remote desktop in the browser streams the screen and input at low delay.

technical_bounds: Needs HTTP/3 server; certificate must be valid or pinned via serverCertificateHashes (self-signed up to 14 days validity)
Datagram payload limited by maxDatagramSize (about 1200 bytes typical)
Safari 26.4 per MDN BCD, later than Chrome 97 and Firefox 114
Subject to the same port blocklist and CSP
